opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though, it was defence of R1 that he has been falsely implicated by the police in the present case,
whereas there was no involvement of his vehicle in the case accident and despite the fact that the FIR was registered against unknown person, he was arrested by the IO on the same day.
However,
the said defence of R1 cannot be taken into consideration, as perusal of criminal case record, as annexed with the DAR, prima facie shows that after receiving information as to the accident, when the IO reached at the spot, he found the offending vehicle at the spot in accidental condition and he also came to know, that the injured has been shifted to BSA Hospital.
Further, as per rukka, when the IO reached at BSA Hospital, the petitioner was not found present at the said hospital, as he was allegedly shifted to Saroj Hospital but, R1 was found present receiving treatment and thereafter, as his vehicle was found present at the spot, therefore, notice U/s 133 of M.V. Act was given to him and in reply to the said notice, R1 admitted involvement of his vehicle in the case accident, on 29.07.2014 itself and thereafter, he was arrested by the IO on the same day.
Thus, merely because the statement of petitioner/injured was recorded on 31.07.2014, the same is not sufficient to give benefit to R1, in proof of his defence of false implication.
21. It was further deposed by R1 that he became aware as to his false implication, only after one year of the case MACT No. 450458/16 Page 20 of38 Deepak vs. Nitin Kumar and Ors. Page 21 of38 accident, and after gaining knowledge of the same, he filed complaint against the IO.
Further, even the arrest memo of R1 was signed by him.
However, even if the said contention of signing the documents,
without knowledge of its contents, is accepted as true on its face value, then also, perusal of present petition reveals that the IO has filed DAR on 09.10.2014 and on the same day, he has produced R1 as driver cum owner of the offending vehicle therefore, as per record, at-least on 09.10.2014, R1 was aware as to his involvement in the present case but, even thereafter, he had not taken any action against the IO and preferred to file the complaint against the IO on 22.07.2015, which appears to be merely an after-thought.
Thus it can be safely concluded that R1 failed to prove his defence.
22. Per contra, PW1 by his unrebutted testimony, which is also duly corroborated by the criminal case record, the MACT No. 450458/16 Page 21 of38 Deepak vs. Nitin Kumar and Ors.
Issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents accordingly.
In view of the findings of this Tribunal, qua issue no.1 regarding rashness and negligence of R1,
resulting in the occurrence of the case accident, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner/claimant is entitled to compensation in respect of medical expenses, special diet charges,
conveyance charge, etc., incurred by him on account of injuries sustained in the above mentioned road traffic accident.
Accordingly, the entitlement of the petitioner to compensation if any, towards special diet and conveyance charges has to be determined in accordance with the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner / victim in the case accident.
However, the petitioner failed to place on record any payment being made by him to any agency,
from which, he had hired any attendant or any document to show credit of any amount to any attendant or agency.
He had also failed to examine any attendant, allegedly hired by him during the said period.
However, taking into consideration the fact that the petitioner has duly proved that as a result of the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries and as his treatment cum MACT No.

during his treatment cum recuperation period of 20 months.
Accordingly, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to award a lump sum amount of Rs. 60,000/-, as compensation to the petitioner, under this head towards attendant charges.
